title: Writing
intro: The prompts your organisation replies with, and when the AI writes with them. Each prompt describes a way of replying; members see its name and its description, not its instructions.
name: Name
whenHint: The AI reads this description to suggest the right prompt for each email.
instructionsHint: Tone, structure, business rules. The common instructions (language of the email, plain text, invent nothing, signature) are added automatically.
correctionsHint: What members changed in this prompt’s proposals, and why. Each one only applies to its author’s proposals: fold into the instructions those that hold for everyone.
usage: {used, plural, one {# reply} other {# replies}}, {edited, plural, =0 {none edited} other {# edited}}
templatesHint: Other ways of replying, ready to add. Once added they are yours to edit.
whichNowAi: Now: the AI sorts your emails, and suggests a prompt for each one to handle.
whichNowNone: Now: the AI does not sort your emails, so no prompt is suggested.
whichSuggested: The AI suggests one, when it sorts
whichMember: A member can always pick another
whichAtFetch: At fetch, the suggested one is used
writingLegend: When the AI writes a proposal
writingNoneHint: Nothing is sent to the AI before.
writingDraftHint: The content of each email to handle is sent to the AI, at most ten per fetch and mailbox.
writingMailboxHint: The same, and the email then moves to Replied, as a draft.
writingNothingSent: Nothing is ever sent to the correspondent without a member’s confirmation.
whichSuggestedText: For each email to handle, from the “when to use it” of each prompt. A rule never suggests a prompt.
whichMemberText: The suggested prompt is preselected and marked. With no suggestion, the first of the list is offered.
whichAtFetchText: With no suggestion, the first prompt of the list.
whichSort: Have the AI sort, in Sorting →
